To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the muon flux and energy spectrum at the NUSEX depth have been measured for the first time and that the observed event distributions are consistent with the standard picture of underground muons.

(i) the average energy of muons is about 1.5 GeV at a depth of 5000 meters water equivalent; (ii) this value is consistent with the theoretical predictions based on the Gaisser-Hillas parameterization and the CORSIKA simulation; (iii) the average energy is consistent with the value obtained by the NUSEX group in 1986; (iv) the energy spectrum is compatible with a power-law distribution with an exponent of -3.
The muon energy spectrum in the NUSEx detector is well described by the usual picture of muon production and propagation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of high energy cosmic rays and their interactions with matter.
the study of the muon energy spectra and their parameters at great depths.
the study of the properties of high-energy cosmic ray muon flux at the NUSEX underground laboratory (4000 mwe, 120 mwev).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in spite of the large experimental and theoretical uncertainties, the present data are compatible with the standard picture of underground muons and the present theoretical calculations.
the present data are in good agreement with the theoretical expectations.
, in the framework of the usual model of muon generation, the NUSEX data are compatible with the theoretical expectations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the muon spectrum shape is well understood and that the observed muon energy spectrum is in agreement with the expectation.
the observed event distributions are well explained by a single power law muon spectrum with an exponent of 2.7.
the NUSEX results are compatible with the standard theoretical expectations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite of the fact that the muon energy is much smaller than the energy of the primary cosmic ray, the energy spectrum of muons in deep underground experiments is still a very important parameter for the understanding of the primary cosmic rays.
the NUSEX muon detector is a good tool for the study of muon properties and the investigation of the cosmic ray composition.
the muon flux is much higher than what we would expect from the standard picture of underground muons.
